content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E042 (Edward Fleming) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities): role is Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time. Recommendation: write.
- Note 6 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommendation: read.

The conflict: employment type. HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Per the access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer owns). So max for full-time = write. Requested write = max, so grant write.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security says basic training, so max = read. Requested write > max, so grant read.

The conflict is between HR (multiple databases say full_time) and Security (contractor). Most databases (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) confirm full_time. Security is the only one saying contractor.

Which should the Approver trust? The notes say note 5 says "Employee is full-time per HR records." Note 6 says Security database shows contractor "differing from HR's full_time note."

Typically, HR is the authoritative source for employment type. Five notes confirm full_time. One note (Security) says contractor. Also note 4 says Compliance database confirms role, employment type per HR/Finance records.

The majority evidence supports full_time. The Security note appears to be outlier. Given the preponderance of evidence, I'd decide the employee is full-time Payroll Specialist, max write, requested write equals max, grant write.

Let me submit decision: write.
